attempts.label: DANDI:001271
attempts.paper_title: Excitation and polarization of isolated neurons by high-frequency sine waves for temporal interference stimulation
attempts.entry_title: Sine wave excitation and tetrodotoxin in isolated neurons (Semenov et al. 2025)
attempts.description: Tests the Figure S2 findings of Semenov, Kim, Silkuniene and Pakhomov (2025) on dandiset 001271, which holds optical membrane potential recordings of 20 cultured hippocampal neurons stimulated by 250-ms, 2-kHz sine waves before and after the solution was replaced by one with tetrodotoxin (6 neurons) or without it (vehicle). Two more notebooks test findings the paper deposited in other dandisets, Figure 3C on 001030 and Figures 1, 2 and S1 on 001032 to 001035 and 001272. The adiabatic heating estimate is recomputed from the paper's values. The strobe imaging of Figures 4 to 6 (001273, 001274) is not tested.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Semenov et al. (2025), Figure S2, from dandiset 001271
Semenov et al. (2025), Figure 3C, from dandiset 001030
Semenov et al. (2025), Figures 1, 2 and S1, from dandisets 001032 to 001035 and 001272

outcomes.statement: The tetrodotoxin experiment was replicated in several neurons, with vehicle controls; the representative traces of Figure S2 come from at least 4 independent replications in different cells.
outcomes.source: Figure S2 legend; Methods, Quantification and statistical analysis
outcomes.quote: Representative traces of the optical membrane potentials were selected from at least 4 and usually 8-15 independent replications in different cells
outcomes.notes: 6 TTX neurons (two on each of 30 July, 31 July and 1 August 2024) and 11 vehicle neurons with a visible solution change, so both readings hold (TTX at least 4, and TTX and vehicle together at least 4). Three more neurons are labelled vehicle but show no gap over 3 minutes. Each subject is one neuron (every session's least similar session of its own subject is more similar than any session of another subject), and all 287 data arrays are distinct.
deviations: The files do not mark the solution change. For TTX neurons it is the first session labelled with TTX; for vehicle neurons it is placed at the last gap of more than 3 minutes between sessions (an assumption; the Methods give 20 to 60 s between sessions and the TTX neurons' gaps before TTX are 3.6 to 10.0 minutes). Three vehicle-labelled neurons have no such gap and count as having no change. Reading (a) does not depend on it.

outcomes.statement: Before the drug, unmodulated 2-kHz sine waves evoked repetitive APs at lower fields and, at the most intense fields, a sustained depolarization in which APs merged into small oscillations.
outcomes.source: Results, Tetrodotoxin blocks sustained depolarization, paragraph 1; Results, Stimulation by 2- and 20-kHz unmodulated sine waves, paragraph 1; Figure S2
outcomes.inferred: The paper states this pattern for Figures 1 and 3 ("At the highest field strengths, multiple APs coalesced into low-amplitude oscillations on top of a continuous depolarization"); for the Figure S2 neurons it is shown only in the traces before the change, and the legend's "abolishes both firing and sustained depolarization" implies both were present before.
outcomes.notes: Each of the 16 combinations of the claims file's readings (O1 to O4) gives not reproduced, and the criterion has no partial outcome; the 8 rows of the whole-frame variant fail too. Firing before the change holds under some readings only. With O1(a) every neuron fires with the 5% height (20 of 20) and 18 or 19 of 20 with the 5-SD height, and 18 to 20 have APs without sustained depolarization at a lower field; with O1(b) all 7 fire with the 5% height and 1 of 7 with the 5-SD height. No neuron shows sustained depolarization (O4) at its highest field under any reading (0 of 20; 0 of 7 under O1(b)), where the criterion needs more than half. At the highest field the mean dF over the last 100 ms of the stimulus is above zero in 20 of 20 neurons (median 2.63%, range 0.55 to 5.41% with O1(a)), below both O4 levels (medians 7.29% and 4.93%), and 9 of the 20 still have an AP in that window. The whole-frame variant finds 1 of 20. Against a baseline without depolarization, the median of the same window over every session after TTX (-0.60%, as in the 5 sham sessions, -0.54 to -1.14%), the highest field raises dF in 20 of 20 neurons by 1.15 to 6.01 points with O1(a), below both O4 levels in every neuron. The depolarization the paper describes is present but smaller than the levels of the claims file's measure, which cannot detect plateaus of this size in these recordings; the failed part says the measure finds none, not that the data show none. The maximum firing rate rises with field in most neurons (tables in the notebook). Whether O4 suits these data is asked of a reader (questions/001271.yaml).
deviations: The files hold 16 x 16 crops and no soma outline, where the paper drew the soma on 64 x 64 images; the claims file's ROI readings O1 were run as written. The Otsu component nearest the centre is often a few pixels of bright membrane, and the 2-pixel erosion of O1(b) is empty in 210 of 287 sessions of 001271, which are dropped from that reading. The whole frame is shown as a variant that decides nothing.

Frames 0 and 1199 of every file are left out of every trace (frame 0 is 1.8 to 8.6 times the mean of the others, the last frame 3 to 8% above the one before), a choice of this attempt; the paper does not mention them.
The three vehicle-labelled neurons with no visible change are included (all their sessions are before any change); without them the outcome is the same (0 or 1 of 17).

outcomes.statement: The sustained depolarization induced by intense unmodulated sine waves reversed immediately when the stimulus ended, so it was not membrane electroporation, which would take seconds or longer to repair.
outcomes.source: Results, Tetrodotoxin blocks sustained depolarization, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: The sustained depolarization induced by intense unmodulated sine waves ( Figures 1 and 3 ) was immediately reversible upon stimulus cessation. It was not related to membrane electroporation, which would take seconds or longer to repair
outcomes.notes: No session qualifies. The criterion judges sessions with sustained depolarization (O4), and under every combination of the claims file's readings there are none, so the claim cannot be tested. The whole-frame variant finds 2 or 3 such sessions under its 5-SD readings, and in each dF falls below the O4 level in both windows after the stimulus. Not judged, at each neuron's highest field dF drops from the last 100 ms of the stimulus to 10 to 40 ms after it in 20 of 20 neurons (median drop 3.04 points), and the next session's F0 is within 10% of the one before in 246 of 262 consecutive pairs.
deviations: The files hold 16 x 16 crops and no soma outline, where the paper drew the soma on 64 x 64 images; the claims file's ROI readings O1 were run as written. The Otsu component nearest the centre is often a few pixels of bright membrane, and the 2-pixel erosion of O1(b) is empty in 210 of 287 sessions of 001271, which are dropped from that reading. The whole frame is shown as a variant that decides nothing.
The claim is tested on the Figure S2 neurons, while the paper's sentence cites Figures 1 and 3 (as the criterion says).

outcomes.statement: 1 uM tetrodotoxin abolished the APs evoked by unmodulated 250-ms, 2-kHz sine waves.
outcomes.source: Results, Tetrodotoxin blocks sustained depolarization, paragraph 1; Figure S2 legend
outcomes.quote: the inhibition of sodium channels with 1 μM tetrodotoxin not only abolished the APs
outcomes.notes: The claims file's readings give different outcomes, and its header blocks a claim when they do. With the O1(a) ROI no AP is found after TTX at the highest common voltage (O5 b, 6 pairs), but over every common voltage (O5 a, 31 pairs) one pair has a single peak after TTX, 19.7 to 21.3% high and 2.8 ms wide, in a 14_20240731 session whose O1(a) ROI is one pixel (pre-stimulus SD 11.8%); these readings find 158 to 204 APs before TTX. With the O1(b) ROI, left with 3 TTX neurons, the 5% height finds peaks 2.0 to 3.9 ms wide after TTX in 9 of 12 pairs, in ROIs whose pre-stimulus SD is about 3 to 12%, and the 5-SD height finds none. In the whole-frame variant no AP is found after TTX in any of 31 pairs under any reading, against 215 to 253 before. The open detail is the soma ROI (methods_unavailable finding). The plotted trace of the one O1(a) AP after TTX is noise (one-pixel ROI, swings of about 40%), and the peak does not pass the session's own 5-SD level (58.9%); no session after TTX has an AP at its own 5-SD level under either claims-file ROI. O3 of the claims file sets the level after TTX from the neuron's sessions before, so the readings are kept as written and still disagree.
deviations: The files hold 16 x 16 crops and no soma outline, where the paper drew the soma on 64 x 64 images; the claims file's ROI readings O1 were run as written. The Otsu component nearest the centre is often a few pixels of bright membrane, and the 2-pixel erosion of O1(b) is empty in 210 of 287 sessions of 001271, which are dropped from that reading. The whole frame is shown as a variant that decides nothing.

Frames 0 and 1199 of every file are left out of every trace (frame 0 is 1.8 to 8.6 times the mean of the others, the last frame 3 to 8% above the one before), a choice of this attempt; the paper does not mention them.
Where a voltage was tested more than once in a phase, APs count when any session has them (a standard choice).

outcomes.statement: Tetrodotoxin also fully blocked the sustained depolarization caused by intense sine waves, consistent with the depolarization arising from repeated activation of voltage-gated sodium channels by the cycling de- and hyperpolarization of the membrane.
outcomes.source: Results, Tetrodotoxin blocks sustained depolarization, paragraph 1; Figure S2 legend
outcomes.quote: Consistent with this hypothesis, the inhibition of sodium channels with 1 μM tetrodotoxin not only abolished the APs but also fully blocked the sustained depolarization
outcomes.notes: The criterion blocks the claim (other) when no TTX neuron has sustained depolarization (O4) before TTX, and none has under any combination of the claims file's readings. In the whole-frame variant one TTX neuron qualifies under the 5-SD level and loses it after TTX. Not judged, the mean dF over the last 100 ms of the stimulus falls after TTX at the same voltage under every reading (whole frame, 31 pairs, 1.31% before against -0.59% after, paired t p = 1.6e-07; O1(a) 1.21% against -0.64%, p = 9.5e-07) and is below zero after TTX at every voltage up to 10 V; in vehicle pairs it falls from 1.80% to 1.55% (p = 0.00054). Before TTX the six TTX neurons' highest fields raise dF by 1.15 to 6.01 points over the after-TTX baseline with O1(a), below both O4 levels in each, so the measure has no depolarization to follow through TTX.
deviations: The files hold 16 x 16 crops and no soma outline, where the paper drew the soma on 64 x 64 images; the claims file's ROI readings O1 were run as written. The Otsu component nearest the centre is often a few pixels of bright membrane, and the 2-pixel erosion of O1(b) is empty in 210 of 287 sessions of 001271, which are dropped from that reading. The whole frame is shown as a variant that decides nothing.

After the change the 5-SD level of O4(a) is the median pre-stimulus SD of the neuron's sessions before the change, as O3 has it for APs, an extension of O3 to O4 assumed by this attempt. It does not change the outcome, as no pair qualifies before TTX.

outcomes.statement: In vehicle controls, recorded about 5 min after the solution was replaced by the same solution without TTX, the firing and sustained depolarization persisted.
outcomes.source: Figure S2 legend; Methods, Quantification and statistical analysis
outcomes.inferred: No sentence states the vehicle result. The Figure S2 legend says the neurons were recorded again after replacement by the same solution "with 1 μM TTX or without it (vehicle control)", the Methods list "vehicle controls in experiments with tetrodotoxin", and the legend's title attributes the loss of firing and depolarization to TTX, which implies the vehicle neurons kept them; Figure S2 shows this in one neuron.
outcomes.notes: The readings of which pairs are compared (O5) disagree. Over every common voltage (O5 a) some pairs with APs before have none after (3 or 4 of 50 to 59 under O1(a), 1 of 9 under O1(b) with the 5% height, 2 of 59 in the whole frame), all near threshold, so the claim fails there; at the highest common voltage (O5 b) every pair keeps its APs under O1(a) with the 5-SD height, and 1 of 11 loses them with the 5% height. No vehicle pair has sustained depolarization (O4) before, so that part is empty. Under O1(a) with the 5% height vehicle neurons fire 334 APs before and 327 after over 59 pairs (p = 0.77). Per neuron, all 11 vehicle neurons fire after the change under O1(a) with the 5% height, and 8 of 11 keep APs in every pair that had them; with the 5-SD height 9 of 11 fire after it and the other two have no AP before either. Placing the change of 13_20240801 at its largest gap (10.8 min, leaving one session before) instead of its last (5.0 min) takes its lost pairs under O1(a) from 1 or 2 to 0, and the O5 readings still disagree in other neurons. The paper does not say which sessions it compared (methods_unavailable finding).
deviations: The files hold 16 x 16 crops and no soma outline, where the paper drew the soma on 64 x 64 images; the claims file's ROI readings O1 were run as written. The Otsu component nearest the centre is often a few pixels of bright membrane, and the 2-pixel erosion of O1(b) is empty in 210 of 287 sessions of 001271, which are dropped from that reading. The whole frame is shown as a variant that decides nothing.

The files do not mark the solution change. For TTX neurons it is the first session labelled with TTX; for vehicle neurons it is placed at the last gap of more than 3 minutes between sessions (an assumption; the Methods give 20 to 60 s between sessions and the TTX neurons' gaps before TTX are 3.6 to 10.0 minutes). Three vehicle-labelled neurons have no such gap and count as having no change. This assumption does not decide the outcome, which is blocked whichever change point 13_20240801 is given.

outcomes.statement: Neurons were selected for APs peaking above 5% dF and lasting about 10 ms; typical APs were 11.3% dF high and 8 ms long, excluding the afterhyperpolarization.
outcomes.source: Methods, Recording of the optical APs and data analyses
outcomes.quote: we selected neurons whose APs peaked at a more than 5% Δ F and lasted about 10 ms (typical values ... 11.3% ± 0.9% Δ F and 8 ± 0.7 ms duration, excluding afterhyperpolarization ... mean ± SEM, n = 22)
outcomes.notes: One of 32 combinations of the claims file's readings (O1 a, F0 over all frames, 5-SD height, first AP of each session, duration to the return to F0) gives means within the paper's SEM (10.76% and 7.62 ms over 18 neurons); the other 31 do not, and the criterion blocks the claim when the readings disagree. With O1(a) mean peaks are 9.29 to 10.82% and widths at half height 3.56 to 4.06 ms (about half the paper's 8 ms); durations to F0 are 6.52 to 9.28 ms. With O1(b) (7 neurons, 1 with the 5-SD height) peaks are 15.8 to 18.9%. In the whole frame peaks are 7.67 to 9.54%. The dataset's neurons are not known to be among the paper's 22.
deviations: The files hold 16 x 16 crops and no soma outline, where the paper drew the soma on 64 x 64 images; the claims file's ROI readings O1 were run as written. The Otsu component nearest the centre is often a few pixels of bright membrane, and the 2-pixel erosion of O1(b) is empty in 210 of 287 sessions of 001271, which are dropped from that reading. The whole frame is shown as a variant that decides nothing.
The paper's 22 neurons are not identified; the 20 neurons of this dataset are used, as the criterion says.

outcomes.statement: Unmodulated 250-ms sine waves at 2 and 20 kHz excited every neuron tested, with APs 100 to 200 ms after onset near threshold, firing rate rising to a ceiling of 60 to 90 Hz, and sustained depolarization at the highest fields.
outcomes.source: Results, Stimulation by 2- and 20-kHz unmodulated sine waves, paragraph 1; Figures 1A to 1C and inset
outcomes.quote: Pure sine waves at 2 and even 20 kHz excited 100% of neurons ... at near-threshold electric field strengths, isolated APs emerged with a delay of 100-200 ms after the sine wave onset ... The maximum firing rate increased linearly until reaching a ceiling of 60-90 Hz
outcomes.notes: No combination of the claims file's readings meets the criterion at both frequencies (0 of 16). The measured value is the 20-kHz excited fraction under the first reading (O1 a, F0 all, 5% height), 88.2% of 17 neurons; at 2 kHz it is 96.4% of 28. The median highest firing rate is 22.2 to 36.7 Hz under O1(a) (54 to 99 Hz needed; 1 to 5 neurons per frequency reach it) and the median first-AP latency at threshold 53.5 to 70.0 ms at 2 kHz and 67.4 to 123.8 ms at 20 kHz (90 to 220 ms needed). Under O1(b) (14 and 10 neurons) the ceilings are 21.7 to 53.9 Hz. Sustained depolarization at the highest field is found in at most one neuron (reported, not judged).
deviations: Tested on DANDI:001032, 001033 and 001035; 001034 duplicates 001032 and is counted once.

The files hold 16 x 16 crops and no soma outline; the claims file's ROI readings O1 were run as written. The 2-pixel erosion of O1(b) leaves pixels in 245 of 624 sessions of 001032, 001033 and 001035; the others are dropped from that reading.
Thresholds and latencies come from the sessions as deposited (the lowest voltage with an AP), not from a threshold search the files record.
outcomes.where: DANDI:001030 and 001032 to 001035 (assigned from their titles; the paper does not map figures to dandisets)

outcomes.statement: All excitation thresholds at 20 kHz were about 2-fold higher than at 2 kHz.
outcomes.source: Results, Excitation thresholds are similar or lower for pure 2- and 20-kHz sine waves than those for modulated sine waves, paragraph 1; Figure 2D
outcomes.quote: All thresholds at 20 kHz were about 2-fold higher than at 2 kHz ( p < 0.0001, two-tailed unpaired t test)
outcomes.notes: 20-kHz thresholds are higher than 2-kHz ones in every reading (pooled p < 0.0001 in 7 of 8 readings), but no reading has all four ratios within 1.8 to 2.2 (6 of 32 stimulus and AP-count rows are), so the criterion fails under every reading. The measured value is the unmodulated 1-AP ratio under the first reading (2.16; 2.15 to 2.19 with the 5% height, 2.56 or 3.51 to 3.53 with the 5-SD height). Unmodulated 5-AP ratios are 2.06 to 2.84 and modulated ones 2.24 to 2.96, from 1 to 3 neurons with modulated 20-kHz thresholds (0 or 1 for 5 APs, where there is no ratio when there are none). Without the 20-kHz sessions of 13_1, which show the cell of 14_1, 0 or 1 of the four ratios is within 1.8 to 2.2 in each reading (a variant). The ratios are of the stated generator voltages; the files say the actual amplitude is smaller by a frequency-dependent factor they do not give, so the field ratio may differ.
deviations: Tested on DANDI:001032, 001033 and 001035; 001034 duplicates 001032 and is counted once.
Thresholds are in stated generator volts; the frequency-dependent calibration to the actual field is not given in the files.

outcomes.statement: Thresholds for sine waves modulated at 20 Hz were significantly higher than for pure sine waves at the same carrier, for 5 APs at 2 kHz and for 1 and 5 APs at 20 kHz, so modulation did not lower excitation thresholds; the 2-kHz unmodulated 1-AP threshold was 57.7 V/cm.
outcomes.source: Results, Excitation thresholds are similar or lower for pure 2- and 20-kHz sine waves than those for modulated sine waves, paragraph 1; Figure 2D; Results, Asymmetric and less-efficient membrane charging, last paragraph
outcomes.quote: thresholds for modulated sine waves, which emulate the TI stimulus at the target, were significantly higher than those for pure sine waves at the same frequency ... p = 0.0079 ... p = 0.0142 and p = 0.0037
outcomes.notes: Under no reading do the three comparisons the paper reports as significant all hold. Modulated thresholds are higher on average wherever they can be compared except at 20 kHz with 1 AP under O1(b) with the 5-SD height (12.00 or 11.93 V unmodulated against 11.00 V for the one modulated neuron). The 2-kHz 5-AP difference is not significant (p = 0.082 to 0.28 under O1(a)), and only 1 to 3 neurons have modulated 20-kHz 1-AP thresholds and 0 or 1 have 5-AP ones (1-AP p = 0.013 with the 5% height under O1(a), 0.80 with the 5-SD height; the 5-AP test cannot be run). Without the 20-kHz sessions of 13_1 the tests fail in every reading too (a variant). The 2-kHz 1-AP threshold is not lower for modulated waves in any reading. The measured value is the mean 2-kHz unmodulated 1-AP threshold under the first reading at 18 V/cm per V, 74.1 V/cm (74.1 to 79.0 under O1(a), 61.2 to 67.6 under O1(b), twice these at the files' 36 V/cm per V), against 57.7 +/- 3.6.
deviations: Tested on DANDI:001032, 001033 and 001035; 001034 duplicates 001032 and is counted once.

Fields use 18 V/cm per stated volt, the scale at which 001271's voltages give the fields of Figure S2; the files state 36 V/cm per V, also shown. The 18 V/cm scale is an assumption of this attempt; the outcome is the same at both scales, so it does not rest on it.
Subject 13_1 of 001032 is counted as one neuron as deposited, though its 20-kHz sessions show another cell; without them the outcome is the same.

outcomes.statement: With 20-Hz modulation, firing above threshold locked to the beats, one AP near the peak of each of the five beats and at most two per beat (ten in all), and modulated sine waves triggered no sustained firing or sustained depolarization.
outcomes.source: Results, Stimulation by 2- and 20-kHz sinusoids modulated at 20 Hz, paragraph 1; Figures 2A and 2B
outcomes.quote: single APs emerged near the peak of each beat, so the firing rate equaled the modulation rate ... the maximum number of APs evoked by five beats was limited to ten. Unlike pure sine waves, modulated stimuli did not trigger sustained firing or sustained depolarization
outcomes.notes: Tested on the criterion as amended after the reader's answer in questions/001271.yaml. The first run, on the header's O4 definition of sustained firing (at least three APs with one in the last 50 ms), was partially_reproduced, assumed. The reader found that the definition misread the paper, which sets modulated firing against the sustained firing of pure sine waves, and amended the criterion. A modulated session now shows sustained firing when more than two APs fall in one beat or, with 5 APs or more, at least as many APs fall outside 12.5 to 37.5 ms of the beats as inside. Under it, 12 of the 16 readings pass, all four O1(a) readings with the 5-SD height and all eight O1(b) readings. Under O1(a) with the 5% height, 91% of 213 APs in 84 modulated sessions fall within 12.5 to 37.5 ms of a beat (49% of 1,383 APs for unmodulated waves), no session has more than 8 APs, all 15 sessions with 5 APs or more have most APs near the beat peaks, no session has as many APs outside that window as inside, and none shows sustained depolarization. The four O1(a) readings with the 5% height fail through a single session, subject 9_2 at 2 kHz and 3.4 V, with three APs in the fifth beat (206.4, 217.4 and 236.2 ms, peaks 11.1 to 22.2% dF). Its pre-onset SD is 9.8% dF, about twice the 5% level, and none of its peaks passes its 5-SD level (49.0% dF); the same neuron's unmodulated session at 3.4 V has a pre-onset SD of 1.40% dF and eight APs of 11.6 to 15.0% dF under both heights. The O4 definition would still flag 15 to 32 modulated sessions under O1(a); the amended rule flags 88 of the 197 unmodulated sessions with 3 APs or more, so it separates the two kinds of wave. What the answer changed is the test of sustained firing, and with it the outcome, from partially_reproduced to reproduced; the first run's assumption that O1(a) decides is no longer needed, as the O1(b) readings pass too.
deviations: Assumed, the 5-SD height decides between the two AP heights of the header (O3), since the readings differ through one session whose pre-onset noise (SD 9.8% dF) is twice the 5% level, so that the 5% height counts noise peaks there as APs.
Tested on DANDI:001032, 001033 and 001035; 001034 duplicates 001032 and is counted once.

outcomes.statement: In the same neuron at the same field strength, pure sine waves triggered more APs than modulated ones, and the threshold was typically lower for unmodulated signals.
outcomes.source: Results, Stimulation by 2- and 20-kHz sinusoids modulated at 20 Hz, paragraph 2; Figures 2A to 2C
outcomes.quote: the threshold was typically lower for unmodulated signals ( Figures 2A - 2C ). At the same field strengths, pure sine waves triggered a larger number of APs
outcomes.notes: All 8 readings of the claims file pass with the 1-AP threshold. With the O1(a) ROI the unmodulated wave gives more APs than the modulated one at the same carrier and voltage in 32 to 43 of 52 pairs (12 neurons) against 2 to 4 (paired t p = 4.7e-10 to 7.8e-07), and the unmodulated 1-AP threshold is lower in 10 to 13 of 12 to 15 neurons (0 to 2 the reverse). With O1(b) (5 neurons) the count is larger in 5 to 14 of 16 pairs against 1 to 3, and the 1-AP threshold lower in 3 to 6 of 3 to 7 neurons against 0 or 1. Requiring the 5-AP threshold too (a variant) passes the four O1(a) readings (2 to 6 of 4 to 9 neurons lower, none the reverse) and fails the four O1(b) ones, which have at most one 5-AP threshold pair. The first run required both thresholds and let O1(a) decide.
deviations: Assumed, "the threshold" is the 1-AP excitation threshold. The paper determined "the minimal voltages eliciting 1 and 5 APs" (Methods, Excitation thresholds are similar or lower for pure 2- and 20-kHz sine waves), and its "excitation thresholds" without a count (Results, Decreased extracellular conductivity lowers excitation thresholds; Figure 3B) are the 1-AP ones, as the fig3b criterion has it. The 5-AP threshold is shown as a variant.
Tested on DANDI:001032, 001033 and 001035; 001034 duplicates 001032 and is counted once.

outcomes.statement: Lowering solution conductivity from 16.4 to 8.4 mS/cm with sodium gluconate reversibly lowered excitation thresholds about 2-fold at all sine wave frequencies from 2 to 20 kHz.
outcomes.source: Results, Decreased extracellular conductivity lowers excitation thresholds, paragraph 1; Figures 3A and 3B
outcomes.quote: Switching to the NaGlu-based solution reversibly and reproducibly decreased excitation thresholds ~2-fold across all sine wave frequencies tested
outcomes.notes: None of the 803 sessions of 001032 to 001035 names the low-conductivity NaGlu solution, and 001030, the only NaGlu dandiset of the paper found, holds 2-s ramped 2-kHz waves in four cells and no NaCl sessions. No 250-ms NaGlu sessions at 2 to 20 kHz were found in any dandiset of the paper's list that was read (001030 to 001035, 001271, 001272); 001031, 001273 and 001274 hold other stimuli by their titles.
deviations: The paper does not say which dandiset holds Figures 3A and 3B; the claims file's assignment (001030, 001032 to 001035) is from titles, and none of them holds the data. Blocked as metadata_insufficient (the data cannot be located from the paper or the archive), since the checker does not allow data_missing for a claim with data elsewhere.
outcomes.where: DANDI:001030 and 001032 to 001035 (assigned from their titles)

outcomes.statement: Excitation by pure sine waves was not caused by heating; the adiabatic temperature rise was 2.5 C after 250 ms at 63 V/cm in NaCl solution, at most 1.24 C for the same stimulus in the low-conductivity solution, and 4.1 C at 81 V/cm in NaCl.
outcomes.source: Results, Decreased extracellular conductivity lowers excitation thresholds, paragraph 2; Figure 3A
outcomes.quote: the maximum theoretical temperature rise (assuming no heat dissipation 43 ) was 2.5°C after 250 ms of near-threshold stimulation at 2 kHz, 63 V/cm, in the NaCl-based solution ... These observations prove that excitation by pure sine waves was not caused by heating
outcomes.notes: Neither reading gives the paper's temperatures (peak field 3.89, 1.99 and 6.44 C; RMS field 1.95, 1.00 and 3.22 C, against 2.5, 1.24 and 4.1 C), while the paper's ratios follow the formula (81 over 63 V/cm within 0.8%, NaGlu over NaCl within 3.2%), which the criterion rules blocked. 2.5 C would need a heat capacity of 6.51 MJ per m3 per K with the peak field or 3.25 with the RMS field, against 4.18 for water.
deviations: Calculated from the paper's values; no data used.
outcomes.where: DANDI:001030 or 001032 to 001035 for the Figure 3A responses (assigned from their titles); the temperatures are calculated from the field, duration and conductivity, not measured

outcomes.statement: In the low-conductivity solution, a 2-s unmodulated 2-kHz sine wave ramped over 250 ms evoked firing for its whole duration, rising with field until replaced by a firing block with sustained depolarization.
outcomes.source: Results, Decreased extracellular conductivity lowers excitation thresholds, paragraph 3; Figure 3C
outcomes.quote: we observed sustained firing for the entire duration of the sine wave ( Figure 3C ). The rate of firing increased with the electric field strength until it was replaced by a firing block and sustained depolarization
outcomes.notes: Each of the 48 combinations of the claims file's readings gives not reproduced, and the criterion has no partial outcome. The first two parts fail only with O1(b) and the 5-SD height; with O1(b) and the 5% height both remaining cells meet both. With O1(a), under every F0, height and bleaching reading, c7 (the cell with six fields, 1.0 to 2.3 V) has APs in the last 250 ms of the 2-s wave at an intermediate field and an AP count that rises from its lowest field; with the 5% height all four cells do, and with the 5-SD height 1 to 3 cells meet the first part and 3 or 4 the second. With O1(b) and the 5-SD height no cell meets the first part. The third part fails in every reading, in the claims file's ROIs and the whole frame. No cell's highest field meets sustained depolarization (O4), so the criterion is not met for one cell or for every cell. In c7 firing drops at 2.3 V (16 APs with O1(a), against 70 to 90 at 1.45 to 2.0 V), with O1(a) its mean dF over the last 250 ms (1.7 to 7.1%) stays below the O4 levels (6.5 to 14.5%), and in the whole frame it is 6.0%, above the 5-SD level, but a single 8.0% peak in the window counts as an AP. The O1(b) ROI leaves two cells, not c7. With bleaching reading (c), a reference smoothed by a 101-ms running median, c7 is corrected under every reading and its mean dF over the last 250 ms at 2.3 V is 6.97 to 7.07%, below the O4 levels (7.93 to 13.28%); the 5-SD level drops little (13.28 against 13.73% with the raw reference under O1(a), F0 all, 5-SD height). In the whole frame reading (c) lets one cell, c8, meet all three parts with F0 over the last 20 ms (a variant). Whether O4, with its no-AP condition, suits the paper's firing block is asked of a reader (questions/001271.yaml).
deviations: Only c7 has an AP-free session for the bleaching correction; for the other cells readings (a) no correction and (b) subtracting c7's 1.0-V trace are both run. Reading (c) subtracts the reference after a 101-ms running median, which keeps the slow bleaching and drops the frame noise and a single AP, so that c7's 1.0-V session can serve when it holds one AP; it is the cell's own AP-free session, else c7 at 1.0 V.
Which neurons are judged is not given (Figure 3C shows one); readings (a) at least one neuron and (b) every neuron with three or more fields are both run and agree.
The c5 recordings at 1.5 and 2.0 V end at 1,914 ms, before the stimulus ends at 2,025 ms; their last-250-ms window is cut to 139 ms.
Tested on DANDI:001030; fields are the stated one-polarity voltages.

outcomes.statement: With Di-8-ANEPPS in place of FluoVolt, in eight neurons, the effects of 2-kHz sine waves were not different, so the excitation by unmodulated sine waves is not a sensitization by FluoVolt.
outcomes.source: Results, Sensitivity to unmodulated sine waves was not caused by FluoVolt dye, paragraph 1; Figure S1
outcomes.quote: Experiments were performed on eight neurons using different electric field strengths tested in a random sequence ... Overall, stimulation effects were not different from those observed with FluoVolt dye
outcomes.notes: DANDI:001272 holds 3 Di-8-ANEPPS neurons (three distinct cells by their images, 65 sessions), where the paper reports eight and the 001272 claims file's count allows no other value, so its figs1-eight-neurons part fails. On the three, under the O1(a) readings, the mean 1-AP threshold is 3.73 to 4.23 V against 4.11 to 4.39 V for 25 to 27 FluoVolt neurons of 001032, 001033 and 001035 (two-sided unpaired t p = 0.72 to 0.93), so no difference is found; the O1(b) ROI is empty in every 001272 session. The next lower voltage tested is 0.5 and 0.2 V below the thresholds of 2_20240806 and 4_20240806; 3_20240806's threshold (2.0 V) is its lowest voltage tested, an upper bound. The three response-pattern claims of the 001272 claims file, which its figs1-effects-same-as-fluovolt also needs, are not run here.
deviations: Only the neuron count and the threshold test of the 001272 claims file are run; its pattern claims (near-threshold delayed APs, shorter delay and sustained firing, sustained depolarization) are not.
Thresholds of the two dyes are compared in stated volts, assuming 001272 and 001032 to 001035 state voltages on the same scale.

outcomes.statement: Membrane charging by 2-us pulses is fast; pooled over 19 experiments, charging and discharging time constants averaged 0.7 and 0.91 us at the cathodic pole and 0.65 and 0.8 us at the anodic pole, so membranes charge fully within each sine wave cycle up to 100 to 200 kHz.
outcomes.source: Results, Kinetics of membrane charging by pulsed electric fields, the paragraph after the Figure 4 legend; Figures 4D and 4E
outcomes.quote: The time constants pooled together for all cells averaged 0.7 ± 0.08 (charging) and 0.91 ± 0.08 (discharging) μs for the cathodic cell pole and 0.65 ± 0.05 and 0.8 ± 0.07 μs for the anodic pole, respectively (mean ± SEM, n = 19)
outcomes.notes: Not attempted in this run. The criterion follows the claims file of DANDI:001273, whose fits (charging and discharging time constants of the cathodic and anodic poles from 2-us strobe images of 512 x 512 pixels, 160 frames per file, 181 files, 10.6 GB) are an analysis of their own; after the other claims the run's five hours left no time to build and check it. Streaming is not the limit (a 59-MB file of 001273 read in 2.3 s).

outcomes.statement: Aligning elongated cells with the field doubled the time constants; the maximum optical TMP and the time constants did not differ between the cathode- and anode-facing poles; and discharging was slower than charging except in elongated cells aligned with the field.
outcomes.source: Results, Kinetics of membrane charging by pulsed electric fields, the paragraph after the Figure 4 legend; Figures 4D and 4E
outcomes.quote: Δ F max did not differ at the cathodic and anodic cell poles, indicating the lack of rectification of the applied electric field ... Aligning elongated cells with the electric field doubled the time constants ... discharging time constants were always larger than the charging ones in the same cell ( p < 0.001, paired t test)
outcomes.notes: Not attempted in this run. The criterion follows the claims file of DANDI:001273, whose fits (charging and discharging time constants of the cathodic and anodic poles from 2-us strobe images of 512 x 512 pixels, 160 frames per file, 181 files, 10.6 GB) are an analysis of their own; after the other claims the run's five hours left no time to build and check it. Streaming is not the limit (a 59-MB file of 001273 read in 2.3 s).

outcomes.statement: FluoVolt sensitivity to 2-kHz sine waves (11.8% per 1 kV/cm) was 42% of that to 2-us pulses (28% per 1 kV/cm) and smaller in every ROI, with sine waves polarizing the two poles more asymmetrically than pulses.
outcomes.source: Results, Asymmetric and less-efficient membrane charging by sine waves compared to pulses, paragraphs 2 to 5; Figures 5, 6B to 6D and S3
outcomes.quote: All numbers were invariably smaller than those measured for the same ROIs with the pulse ( Figure 6D ). The electric field sensitivity averaged across all ROIs in all the cells was 11.8% ± 1.7% per 1 kV/cm, just 42% of the value for the 2-μs pulses
outcomes.notes: Not attempted in this run. The criterion follows five claims of the claims file of DANDI:001274 (per-ROI field sensitivity to 2-us pulses and to sine waves from strobe images, 232 files, 25.0 GB), an analysis of its own that the run's time did not allow after the other claims. Streaming is not the limit (a 116-MB file read in 4.0 s).

outcomes.statement: The 2-kHz AP threshold of 57.7 V/cm times the sine wave sensitivity gives a 0.68% emission change, about 6.8 mV, so the threshold depolarization is 5 to 15 mV, as with intracellular current injection.
outcomes.source: Results, Asymmetric and less-efficient membrane charging by sine waves compared to pulses, last paragraph
outcomes.quote: This threshold corresponds to a 0.68% ± 0.11% FluoVolt emission change (11.8 × 57.7/1,000) ... a 0.68% emission change corresponds to a 6.8-mV depolarization at the AP threshold
outcomes.notes: Depends on fig6-sine-less-than-pulse, which is blocked (other), so it is blocked for the same reason. Its other input, the mean 2-kHz unmodulated 1-AP threshold, is 74.1 V/cm under the first reading here (fig2d-modulated-thresholds-higher), against the paper's 57.7.
outcomes.where: DANDI:001032 to 001035 for the threshold and DANDI:001274 for the sensitivity (assigned from their titles)

findings.statement: DANDI:001271 states in every file that 1 V translates to 36 V/cm, but its stated voltages give the fields marked in Figure S2 at 18 V/cm per V (45, 63, 72; 90, 108, 117; 54, 72, 81 V/cm match neurons tested at 2.5, 3.5, 4; 5, 6, 6.5; 3, 4, 4.5 V before and after the change) and at no voltages at 36 V/cm per V. The voltages are likely peak-to-peak, which the 001271 descriptions do not say (001032 to 001035 say peak-to-peak; 001030 says one polarity).

The descriptions of the 71 TTX sessions of DANDI:001271 say TTX abolished the action potentials and "caused sustained depolarization during application of stimulating waves". The paper and the dandiset's own description say TTX prevented it, and the data agree with them (mean dF over the last 100 ms of the stimulus below zero after TTX at every voltage up to 10 V).

DANDI:001271 does not mark the solution change. Sessions before it carry the same label, "without tetrodotoxin (vehicle control)", as vehicle sessions after it; the change of the 11 vehicle neurons was placed from gaps between session start times, and 3 vehicle-labelled neurons (13_20240731, 17_20240801, 4_20240730) show no such gap.

The files of 001271, 001272 and 001032 to 001035 hold 16 x 16 frames, where the paper describes 64 x 64 images after 4 x 4 binning, with no soma ROI, no stimulus record and no stimulus onset; the timing (50 ms onset, 250 ms) is from the Methods and agrees with the aliased stimulus at 10 and 12 V (52 to 299 ms) and with the AP times.

In every file of 001271, 001030 and 001032 to 001035 the first frame is 1.5 to 24 times brighter than the rest and the last frame a few percent brighter than the one before, which no description mentions.

All 178 data arrays of DANDI:001034 are identical to those of DANDI:001032, with the same start times, under other subject identifiers (1_3 for 1_1 and so on); the same recordings are deposited twice as parts 1 and 3.

Some subjects of DANDI:001032 hold sessions of more than one cell. The 20-kHz sessions of 13_1 show the same image as the sessions of 14_1 (correlation 0.997) and correlate 0.09 with 13_1's 2-kHz sessions; 9 subjects of 001032, 001033 and 001035 have pairs of sessions whose mean frames correlate below 0.8.

In DANDI:001030 each file is its own subject, named by cell and voltage (c7_1,0V is cell 7 at 1.0 V, not 0 V), so the four cells are identified only by the file names; two c5 recordings (1.5 and 2.0 V) end at 1,914 ms, before the 2-s stimulus ends.
DANDI:001272 holds 3 Di-8-ANEPPS neurons, where the paper reports experiments on eight.
No 250-ms recordings in the low-conductivity NaGlu solution (Figures 3A and 3B) were found in the paper's dandisets read here (001030 to 001035, 001271, 001272).

The descriptions of 001032 to 001035 say the actual amplitude is smaller than the stated voltage by frequency-dependent calibration factors "reported separately"; the factors are not in the dandisets, so fields at 2 and 20 kHz cannot be compared exactly. 001030 and 001032 to 001035 do not name the paper in their metadata, and the paper does not say which figure is in which dandiset.

Question for the paper's authors. How was the soma ROI drawn on the deposited 16 x 16 crops, which the soma nearly fills (the whole crop, or an outline), and by what rule were APs counted? The claims file's Otsu ROIs are often a few pixels of membrane, and the outcome of figs2-ttx-abolishes-aps, figs2-vehicle-keeps-response and ap-amplitude-duration depends on this choice; the whole frame gives no AP after TTX in any of 31 pairs. The AP height level matters too, for fig2-modulated-locks-to-beats through one noisy session (pre-onset SD 9.8% dF), where a fixed 5% dF level counts three APs in one beat and a 5-SD level counts none.

Question for the paper's authors. How was sustained depolarization measured? The plateaus in 001271 at the highest field are 0.6 to 5.4% dF (median 2.6%) with small oscillations, below the claims file's levels (5 pre-stimulus SD, or half the AP height, with no AP in the last 100 ms), so that no session qualifies and four claims are blocked or fail on it.

Question for the paper's authors. Which session pairs were compared before and after the vehicle change (every field, or the highest), which APs and which duration measure give 11.3% and 8 ms, and which heat capacity and field (peak or RMS) give 2.5 C at 63 V/cm? Each choice changes an outcome here.

verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The three executed notebooks with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the paper. The handover gave the verifier the claims file of DANDI:001272 in place of this entry's claims/001271 file: tools/entry.py handover copies every claims file of the entry's dandisets under its file name, and both are named 10.1016-j.xcrp.2025.102660.yaml. The verifier judged the 19 claims of the 001272 file; eleven of their ids are also in the 001271 file (with criteria that differ in wording), and the claims only in the 001271 file it could not check against a criterion. Results below are given per claim of the 001271 file.

disagreements.reason: Not judged. The claims file the verifier was given does not contain this id, and its 001271 claim ids "cannot be checked against any criterion I have".

Not judged (not in the claims file given). Point B3 bears on it. O6 sustained depolarization is practically never met in this dataset; the 5-SD level (median 7.3%) is above the observed plateaus (2 to 5%) and the traces drift negative from bleaching, so every sustained-depolarization claim ends as none qualify or not reproduced. This is the claims file's measure applied literally, but the notebook should say that the measure cannot detect the effect here, not that the data contradict it. It asked for a per-neuron table of last-100-ms dF against the levels at the highest voltage, split by group, with bleaching-matched sham or low-field traces.
Not judged (not in the claims file given). Point B3 applies (see figs2-before-firing-then-depolarization).

Judged within the 001272 file's figs2-ttx-blocks-depolarization (partially_reproduced). Under O1(a) the APs are gone after TTX in 30 of 31 same-voltage pairs; the one exception is a single 21% peak, 2.8 ms wide, in a session whose pre-onset SD is 11.8% (14_20240731 at 4.0 V). O1(b) leaves only 2 to 28 pixels and its noise passes the 5% level (9 of 12 pairs). B2: after the solution change the 5-SD AP level is the neuron's median pre-change SD, not the session's own; the O3 in the verifier's file does not say this, so it is the attempt's own choice, and it lets a noise spike count as an AP (level 10.1% instead of 59%), turning the claim from reproduced to not reproduced under O1(a)/5sd. B4: O1(b) is empty in 210 of 287 sessions and its 2 to 28 pixel ROIs split most readings-differ outcomes, a defect of the reading on 16 x 16 data. It asked for plots of that raw trace.

Judged within the 001272 file's figs2-ttx-blocks-depolarization. All 11 vehicle neurons still fire afterwards; 4 of 59 pairs lose their APs. B6: every non-TTX session is labelled vehicle control, so the split is inferred from a gap over 3 minutes, and for 13_20240801 the last such gap (5.0 min) is not its largest (10.8 min). It asked for per-neuron vehicle results.
Not judged (not in the claims file given). Point B4 on O1(b) applies.
Not judged (not in the claims file given).

No cell's highest field meets sustained depolarization under any reading or bleaching option. B5, the bleaching correction subtracts a raw single trace, which raises the pre-onset SD by about 1.4 times and with it the 5-SD level (c7 at 2.3 V, 7.08% against 13.7%), and excludes c7's 1.0-V session as a reference because of one AP, so c7 goes uncorrected under otsu/5pct. Under half_ap the margin is small (7.08 against 8.80).

verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The three full executed notebooks of the round-1 revision, with their conclusions and summaries, the helper module, the attempt record and the claims file of DANDI:001271 (claims/001271), with the paper.

disagreements.reason: Every one of the 24 claims-file readings returns "not reproduced" (cell 26), and the criterion has no partial outcome. The "firing part" the record says holds also depends on the reading: with O1(a) and the 5-SD height only 18 or 19 of 20 neurons have APs, with O1(b) and the 5-SD height only 1 of 7. The sentences "Firing holds ... under every combination of the claims file's readings" (record) and "So the firing part holds" (cell 33) are not supported. The outcome should be not_reproduced, with the note that the claims file's measure cannot detect plateaus of this size. O4 requires no AP in the last 100 ms, while the paper describes APs that "coalesced into low-amplitude oscillations on top of a continuous depolarization"; a detector at 5% counts those oscillations as APs (9 of 20 neurons at their highest field), so O4 rules out by construction the state the paper describes, and the claims file should revise it.

The notebook's own tally is "not reproduced" in 48 of 48 readings (cell 11). The first two parts hold only with the O1(a) ROI; with O1(b) and the 5-SD height no cell meets the first part. The third part fails everywhere. Cell 15 says "with the 5-SD height 1 to 3 cells meet each part", but with the smoothed bleaching reference 4 cells meet the "rises" part. Its outcome is also decided by the O4 issue, which the claims file should revise.

entries.name: 001048-semenov-2025
entries.title: High-frequency sine waves excite isolated neurons (Semenov et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Semenov, Kim, Silkuniene and Pakhomov (2025). Dandiset 001048 names the paper but holds HEK-cell recordings of another study, so the claims are tested on the ten dandisets the paper lists (001030 to 001035, 001271 to 001274). These hold optical recordings of rat hippocampal neurons stimulated by unmodulated and 20-Hz modulated sine waves at 2 and 20 kHz, with TTX and Di-8-ANEPPS controls, and strobe images of membrane charging by 2-us pulses and sine waves.

entries.name: 001271-semenov-2025
entries.title: Sine wave excitation and tetrodotoxin in isolated neurons (Semenov et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the Figure S2 findings of Semenov, Kim, Silkuniene and Pakhomov (2025) on dandiset 001271, which holds optical membrane potential recordings of 20 cultured hippocampal neurons stimulated by 250-ms, 2-kHz sine waves before and after the solution was replaced by one with tetrodotoxin (6 neurons) or without it (vehicle). Two more notebooks test findings the paper deposited in other dandisets, Figure 3C on 001030 and Figures 1, 2 and S1 on 001032 to 001035 and 001272. The adiabatic heating estimate is recomputed from the paper's values. The strobe imaging of Figures 4 to 6 (001273, 001274) is not tested.
